diagnosis.hypothesis: Baseline validation showed user1→web1 and user1→app1 at 100% loss, and web1→user1/app1→user1 producing ICMP redirects toward 10.10.50.10 (app1). Inspection of leaf2's static routes found the route 10.10.10.0/24 pointing to next-hop-group ibn-wrt-m1 (single next-hop 10.10.50.10 = app1 host on the server VLAN), instead of the fabric p2p group to-leaf1 used by its sibling 10.10.20.0/24 and 10.10.99.0/24 routes. Repointed leaf2's 10.10.10.0/24 next-hop-group to to-leaf1 (fabric p2p 10.255.0.4/10.255.0.6). Post-fix public_success_criteria validation: all 10 lab_connectivity pairs pass (0% loss, no redirects).
diagnosis.reference: On leaf2, the static route to 10.10.10.0/24 (toward user1 in users_vlan) points to the wrong next hop 10.10.50.10, an address on the wrong egress instead of the path via leaf1.

commands: network-instance default route-table ipv4-unicast route 10.10.10.0/24 { admin-state enable next-hop-group to-leaf1 }
changes.reason: leaf2's route to users_vlan 10.10.10.0/24 uses next-hop-group ibn-wrt-m1 (10.10.50.10, the app1 host), so leaf2 sends user-bound traffic to app1, which issues ICMP redirects and the user1 path fails. It should use the to-leaf1 group (10.255.0.4/10.255.0.6 fabric p2p) to reach leaf1, as the sibling routes to-leaf1 already do for 10.10.20/99.
rollback_commands: network-instance default route-table ipv4-unicast route 10.10.10.0/24 { admin-state enable next-hop-group ibn-wrt-m1 }
